title: Quantum telescopy with realistic anti-correlated optical fields as references
abstract: Quantum telescopy, proposed by Grottesman et al., uses spatially entangled single-photon states to modify HBT stellar interferometry, potentially surpassing Michelson interferometry in resolution without baseline limits. However, finite source bandwidth, non-unit efficiency, detector response times, and celestial light bandwidth all affect its effectiveness. In this work, we consider a spatially entangled singe-photon state generated by beam-splitting a practical anti-bunched photon source from resonance fluorescence, which is a common method of generating single-photon states, and evaluate the signal level in quantum telescopy with inclusion of imperfection of detection system and finite bandwidth of celestial light. Here, given the incoming light, we optimize the parameters of the anti-bunched photon source and the detector system for the best signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), which can match that of the Michelson method in the ideal case but is always smaller in the realistic case. Alternatively, weak coherent states from heavily attenuated lasers can replace the entangled single-photon state but suffer low signal level, similar to HBT method. We find that the SNR with a realistic anti-bunched source for producing the reference fields can still beat the SNR of the coherent state scheme in the weak incoming field limit. The optimized parameters for the anti-bunched source and detection system will be a guide for future experimental endeavor.
summary: This paper analyzes quantum telescopy, a technique for enhancing astronomical resolution using entangled photons. It compares the achievable Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) when using realistic anti-bunched sources versus idealized or coherent state references. The key finding is that even with imperfections, the anti-bunched source method maintains a significant advantage over coherent state references in the weak light regime.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve the angular resolution in optical astronomy beyond the diffraction limit by utilizing quantum telescopy techniques.
main_result: The Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) using a realistic anti-bunched source can still outperform the coherent state scheme in the weak incoming field limit, guiding future experimental optimization.
method: The analysis involves deriving and optimizing the SNR for quantum interferometry by considering realistic imperfections like finite bandwidth and detector efficiency.
model_or_system: The system models quantum telescopy using spatially entangled single-photon states generated from practical anti-bunched sources (like resonance fluorescence) as references for stellar interferometry.
key_observables: Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), Visibility (V), and Coincidence count rate (Rc).
important_parameters: Weak incoming field limit ($N_R \ll 1$), detector efficiency ($\eta$), and source correlation parameters ($ eta, \Omega$).
main_assumptions: Assumes incoming fields and reference fields are uncorrelated, and makes approximations regarding the asymptotic behavior of correlation functions for weak fields.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between traditional HBT, phase-sensitive HBT with coherent references, and the use of entangled single-photon states as references.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by detailing the phase-dependent HBT effect, incorporating practical constraints, analyzing anti-bunched sources from resonance fluorescence, deriving the SNR formula, and finally optimizing parameters.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical framework for optimizing quantum measurements in quantum optics, specifically addressing the practical limitations of using non-ideal quantum sources for high-precision sensing.
